unit: Algebra · Chapter 1. Properties of numerical functions
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 9 mathematics textbooks

stages.headline: A function increases on an interval if f(x) grows as x grows, and decreases if f(x) gets smaller.
stages.headlineEnglish: A function increases on an interval if f(x) grows as x grows, and decreases if f(x) gets smaller.

stages.headline: Zeros of a function are the x where f(x) = 0 — where the graph meets Ox; between zeros the function keeps its sign.
stages.headlineEnglish: Zeros of a function are the x where f(x) = 0 — where the graph meets Ox; between zeros the function keeps its sign.

stages.headline: The greatest (least) value of a function is the largest (smallest) of its values; y = x² − 4 has least value −4.
stages.headlineEnglish: The greatest (least) value of a function is the largest (smallest) of its values; y = x² − 4 has least value −4.

stages.headline: Zero and sign intervals of f(x) = 2x − 6?
stages.headlineEnglish: Zero and sign intervals of f(x) = 2x − 6?
stages.problemText: Zero and sign intervals of f(x) = 2x − 6?
stages.correctAnswer: x = 3; f < 0 when x < 3, f > 0 when x > 3
stages.customInstructions: The zero and both sign intervals are required.
